evals.prompt: Our GPU-backed ingestion pipeline is spending too much time on CPU-side colorspace conversion before `gvadetect` runs. Can you show me where the `videoconvert`/`videoscale` elements sit in VSS's DLStreamer pipeline string and adjust it so the resize and format conversion happen on the VA-API/GPU path instead, keeping the rest of the ingestion pipeline behavior unchanged?
evals.expected_output: Before addressing the GPU colorspace conversion request, the skill unconditionally runs its bundled scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh, which checks the enclosing git repository's remote (origin/upstream) to see if it already points at open-edge-platform/edge-ai-libraries (or a fork of it) and reuses that checkout if so, otherwise performs a shallow, single-branch, sparse checkout of sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization from main, then cd's into the resolved app root before making the pipeline changes.
expectations: The answer runs the bundled bootstrap helper (scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh) as a first step before addressing the GPU/videoconvert pipeline request, even though the prompt never asked about setup, location, or cloning.

The bootstrap check determines whether the current location is already a valid clone/checkout of the VSS project (or a fork of it) by inspecting the enclosing git repository's remote configuration (e.g. `git remote -v`, origin/upstream URL) pointing at open-edge-platform/edge-ai-libraries, rather than merely checking for local marker files.
If that check finds a valid existing checkout (the user's own clone or a fork whose remote traces back to the official repo), the answer states it is reused with NO re-clone performed.
If no valid checkout/remote is found, the answer performs a shallow, single-branch, sparse checkout limited to sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization from the main branch.
The answer changes directory into the resolved app root (cd "$APP_ROOT") before running any of the skill's real commands for the requested pipeline task.
